title: Typed embedded adapters in supervised workers
contractChanges: Protocol v1 over the fork IPC channel, 8 MiB message ceiling.
CanonicalAnchor gained relativePath: a live read has no CapturedManifest to resolve a FileId back to a path, and every consumer needs one.

tests.name: test/contracts/worker-lifecycle.test.js
tests.detail: 7/7: cancellation releases the caller without killing the worker; an abandoned job's late answer is discarded; a crash is typed and retryable and the next call gets a new pid; an oversized response is a bound, not a truncation; stdout cannot forge protocol; an unknown operation does not kill the worker; an expired budget never reaches the worker

tests.name: test/contracts/retrieval-adapter.test.js
tests.detail: real zvec library, real worker, real crash and cancel

tests.name: test/contracts/graph-adapter.test.js
tests.detail: real indexed project, typed call paths, byte anchors, one handle per workspace

findings: Protocol travels on the fork IPC channel, never stdout. Proven: a worker that prints a protocol-shaped object on stdout cannot forge a response.
The zvec read API has no AbortSignal, so cancellation is modelled as caller release plus job abandonment plus worker recycling past a threshold. Nothing pretends the call aborts.
CodeGraph's OpenOptions.readOnly is declared but never forwarded to the database, and open runs migrations and healing. The graph worker therefore enforces exactly one handle per workspace.
The typed path surfaces zvec's diagnostics.emptyReason, which the CLI text path could not see: a genuine zero-hit is now `empty` instead of an opaque block.
knownLimitations: The design named workers/graph/main.cjs; it is main.mjs because @lazy-intel/core is ESM. CodeGraph's CommonJS build is loaded with createRequire.
rollback: Unset LAZY_INTEL_ENGINE. The legacy adapters are untouched.
